question: Under the Oklahoma Real Estate License Code, when may the Oklahoma Real Estate Commission place a licensee's license on inactive status at the licensee's own request?
choice_a: Only during the licensee's first license term
choice_b: Only if the licensee has no pending disciplinary complaints
choice_c: Automatically at the end of each 36-month license term
choice_d: When the request is in writing, accompanied by sufficient reason, on Commission forms
explanation: The Commission may place a license on inactive status when the written request is accompanied by sufficient reason, submitted on forms furnished by the Commission; inactive status does not relieve the licensee of paying required fees.

question: A licensee requests inactive status while on active military service. According to the License Code, what is different about this request compared to a routine voluntary inactive request?
choice_a: The licensee is not required to pay the fees otherwise due, but must request inactive status prior to each license term
choice_b: The license automatically converts to a broker license
choice_c: The licensee is exempt from ever reactivating the license
choice_d: The branch office license is automatically revoked
explanation: During active military service, a licensee is not required to pay the license fees but must request inactive status prior to each term for which the license is to be issued.

question: Besides a voluntary request, under what other circumstance must the Commission place a license on inactive status?
choice_a: Whenever a licensee changes employing brokers
choice_b: When a licensee fails to comply with all Code and Rule requirements for active status, including a Commission request for documentation
choice_c: Whenever a licensee moves to a new county
choice_d: Only if ordered by a district court
explanation: A licensee who at any time fails to comply with all Code and Rule requirements for active status shall be placed on inactive status, including failure to comply with a Commission request for documentation tied to a statutory or rule requirement. The license returns to active status once the licensee complies.

question: Does the continuing education requirement of Section 858-307.2 apply while a real estate license is on inactive status?
choice_a: Yes, inactive licensees must still complete the full continuing education hours every term
choice_b: Only sales associates are exempt, brokers are not
choice_c: No, the continuing education requirement does not apply during the period a license is on inactive status
choice_d: Only if the licensee has been inactive for more than three years
explanation: Section 858-307.2 expressly exempts a license from the continuing education requirement during the period it is on inactive status; the requirement instead attaches as a condition of renewal or reactivation.

question: What fee must accompany a request to activate or reissue a license, in addition to any required documentation, under Commission rule?
choice_a: Two Hundred Dollars ($200.00)
choice_b: No fee is required to reactivate a license
choice_c: Seven Dollars and fifty cents ($7.50)
choice_d: Forty Dollars ($40.00)
explanation: All requests for activation or re-issuance of a license must be accompanied by the appropriate documents and a Forty Dollar ($40.00) fee; a licensee who paid the reduced inactive fee rate must also pay the remaining active fee.

question: How many clock hours of Commission-approved continuing education must a licensee show, as a condition of activation or active reinstatement, absent an exemption?
choice_a: Thirty (30) clock hours
choice_b: Fifteen (15) clock hours
choice_c: Ninety (90) clock hours
choice_d: Forty-five (45) clock hours
explanation: As a condition of activation or active reinstatement, a licensee must provide evidence of completion of thirty (30) clock hours of Commission-approved continuing education, or its equivalent, subject to the statutory exemptions.

question: A broker's license lapsed during the previous license term. Before that broker's license may be reinstated or reactivated, what must the broker complete in addition to elective hours?
choice_a: Nothing extra; brokers are exempt from continuing education on reinstatement
choice_b: The Broker in Charge course and six (6) hours of Contracts and Forms education
choice_c: A brand-new 90-hour prelicense course
choice_d: Only the national criminal history background check
explanation: A broker who lapsed or renewed inactive in the previous or current license term must complete the Broker in Charge course, six (6) hours of Contracts and Forms education, and nine (9) hours of elective courses before reinstatement or reactivation.

question: As defined in the Commission's rules, what does "inactive status" mean for a licensee?
choice_a: A period in which a licensee may still list and sell property but not collect commissions
choice_b: A temporary suspension imposed only as discipline for a violation
choice_c: A period in which a licensee is prohibited from performing activities that require an active license
choice_d: A status available only to sales associates, not brokers
explanation: The rules define "inactive status" as a period during which a licensee is prohibited from performing activities which require an active license.

question: According to the Commission's rules, what is a "branch office"?
choice_a: Any office a licensed associate personally maintains independent of the broker
choice_b: A temporary pop-up location used only for open houses
choice_c: An office maintained by a home-warranty or title company on the broker's behalf
choice_d: An extension of a broker's main office location, normally at a different location, which shall not be independently owned by any person other than the applicable broker or entity
explanation: A branch office is defined as an extension of a broker's main office location, normally located at a different location than the main office, and it shall not be independently owned by any person other than the applicable broker or entity.

question: A real estate broker wants to conduct business from a second location that is an extension of the main office. What must the broker do under Title 59?
choice_a: Obtain a branch office license for that additional location, with the office under the direction and supervision of a separate broker who is considered its managing broker
choice_b: Nothing, as long as the same broker signs all contracts
choice_c: Register the location only with the county clerk
choice_d: Wait until the license renewal term to add the location
explanation: If a broker maintains more than one place of business that is an extension of the main office, a branch office license must be obtained for each additional location, and each branch office must be under the direction and supervision of a separate broker considered the managing broker of that branch office.

question: Under Commission rule, who must a broker designate to act as broker for, and supervise the activities of, each branch office location?
choice_a: The broker must always personally act as branch broker at every location
choice_b: A branch broker, other than the broker personally (unless the branch office is at the same location as the main office)
choice_c: The most senior sales associate at that office, regardless of license type
choice_d: Any unlicensed office manager approved by the Commission
explanation: A broker shall designate a branch broker, other than himself or herself, to act as broker for each branch location and supervise its activities; a broker may act as branch broker only if the branch office is located at the same location as the main office, upon the appropriate filings.

question: What responsibility does a designated branch broker bear for the associates assigned to that branch office?
choice_a: None; only the main-office broker is responsible
choice_b: The branch broker is responsible only for associates who are also broker associates
choice_c: The branch broker assumes responsibility, in conjunction with the broker, for all associates assigned to the branch office
choice_d: Responsibility passes entirely to the branch broker, releasing the main broker
explanation: The branch broker assumes responsibility, in conjunction with the broker, for all associates assigned to the branch office; the branch broker may also be authorized to perform duties and sign documents on the broker's behalf for that branch.

question: A branch office's designated branch broker suddenly dies, and the branch office is to continue doing business. What must the main office broker do?
choice_a: Immediately close the branch office permanently
choice_b: Personally take over supervision with no filing required
choice_c: Wait until the next license renewal to name a replacement
choice_d: Appoint a new branch broker and file the appropriate documents with the Commission within thirty (30) days of the event
explanation: In the event of the death, disability, retirement, or cessation of employment of the designated branch broker, if the branch office is to continue business, the main office broker must appoint a new branch broker and file the appropriate documents with the Commission within thirty (30) days of the occurrence.

question: Can a branch office operate under a trade name different from the main office's name?
choice_a: Yes, so long as the broker registers the trade name(s) with the Commission
choice_b: No, a branch office must always use the identical name of the main office
choice_c: Only if the branch office is in a different county
choice_d: Only sole proprietorships may use a different branch trade name
explanation: A branch office may utilize a trade name different from the main office, provided the broker registers the name(s) with the Commission.

question: A real estate corporation seeks a real estate business entity license from OREC. Which of the following is a required element under Commission rule?
choice_a: Every shareholder of the corporation must individually hold a sales associate license
choice_b: The corporation must have a managing corporate broker who holds a separate license as a real estate broker
choice_c: The corporation must waive its right to conduct business under a trade name
choice_d: The corporation must be headquartered in Oklahoma City
explanation: To obtain a real estate business entity license, a corporation or association must, among other things, have a managing corporate broker who holds a separate license as a real estate broker, and must demonstrate good standing to transact business in Oklahoma.

question: How is a corporation's managing broker designation established under Commission rule?
choice_a: By a verbal agreement among the board of directors
choice_b: By a public notice published in a local newspaper
choice_c: By sworn statement signed by the President of the corporation or authorized member/manager of the association, stating the date and place the designation occurred
choice_d: By the individual broker simply notifying the Commission by phone
explanation: The designation of a managing broker for a corporation or association shall be established by a sworn statement signed by the President of the corporation, or authorized member or manager of the association, stating the date and place such action was effected.

question: A corporation's managing broker retires and ceases employment with the firm. What must the corporation do, and by when?
choice_a: Nothing is required as long as another broker eventually takes over
choice_b: Surrender its business entity license within twenty-four (24) hours
choice_c: Notify the Secretary of State only; OREC notification is optional
choice_d: Appoint a new managing broker and file notice of the change with the Commission no later than thirty (30) days after the event, along with required documents and fee
explanation: Upon the death, disability, retirement, or cessation of employment of the managing broker, the corporation or association must appoint a new managing broker and file the notice of change with the Commission no later than thirty (30) days after the event, accompanied by required documents and a $40.00 change-of-status fee.

question: Who is responsible for the acts of associates associated with a real estate business entity such as a corporation?
choice_a: The managing broker, in conjunction with the corporation, association, or business entity, is responsible for all acts of the entity, including the acts of all associates
choice_b: Only the individual associate who committed the act
choice_c: The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission itself bears vicarious liability
choice_d: No one; entity licenses eliminate individual liability entirely
explanation: The managing broker, in conjunction with the corporation, association, or business entity, is responsible for all acts of the business entity, including the acts of all associates associated with the entity.

question: What minimum broker staffing does a partnership need in order to be licensed as a real estate business entity?
choice_a: One managing partner who holds a sales associate license
choice_b: A minimum of two managing partners who each hold a separate license as a real estate broker
choice_c: No individually licensed partner is required if the partnership itself is registered
choice_d: At least five licensed sales associates
explanation: A partnership seeking a real estate broker license as a business entity must have a minimum of two managing partners, each of whom holds a separate license as a real estate broker.

question: If a partnership loses one of its managing partners to death or retirement, what happens to the partnership's license under Commission rule, absent a contrary partnership agreement?
choice_a: The partnership continues automatically with no filing required
choice_b: The Commission automatically appoints a replacement managing partner
choice_c: The partnership is dissolved, unless the partnership agreement provides for continuation, in which case a new managing partner must be appointed and reported within thirty (30) working days
choice_d: The partnership converts automatically into a sole proprietorship
explanation: Upon the death, disability, retirement, or cessation of employment of a managing partner, the partnership is dissolved unless the partnership agreement provides otherwise; if it provides for continuation, the partnership must appoint a new managing partner and file notice with the Commission within thirty (30) working days.

question: What happens to a sole proprietor real estate firm upon the death, disability, or retirement of the sole proprietor broker?
choice_a: The firm automatically transfers to the most senior associate
choice_b: The firm converts automatically to a corporation
choice_c: The Commission appoints an interim broker to continue operations
choice_d: The sole proprietor firm shall cease business activities
explanation: Because a sole proprietorship has no separate legal entity or successor broker built into its licensure, the rule provides that the sole proprietor firm shall cease business activities upon the death, disability, or retirement of the sole proprietor.

question: What must a real estate broker maintain as a "place of business" under Commission rule?
choice_a: At least one enclosed room or building of stationary construction where transactions can be negotiated and closed with privacy, and where books, records, and files are maintained
choice_b: A P.O. Box is sufficient with no physical location
choice_c: Any coffee shop the broker regularly frequents
choice_d: A virtual office listed only on the broker's website
explanation: Each broker's place of business must consist of at least one enclosed room or building of stationary construction where negotiations and closings can be conducted with privacy and where the broker's books, records, and files pertaining to real estate transactions are maintained.

question: May an associate (sales associate or broker associate) maintain their own separate place of business apart from their sponsoring broker?
choice_a: Yes, any associate may register their own office with the Commission
choice_b: No, associates are not permitted to have a place of business; they must be registered with a place of business maintained and registered in the name of the broker
choice_c: Only broker associates may maintain a separate office
choice_d: Yes, but only if it is within the same city as the broker's office
explanation: Associates are not permitted to have their own place of business; they must instead be registered with a place of business that is maintained and registered in the name of their broker.

question: Under Commission rule, is a broker responsible for the real estate-related activities of an unlicensed assistant working within the firm?
choice_a: No, unlicensed assistants fall entirely outside OREC's jurisdiction
choice_b: Only if the unlicensed assistant is being paid a commission
choice_c: Yes, a broker is responsible for all real estate-related activities of any unlicensed assistant working within the firm
choice_d: Responsibility shifts to the unlicensed assistant's direct supervisor if not the broker
explanation: A broker is responsible for all real estate-related activities of any unlicensed assistant working within the firm, reinforcing the broker's overall supervisory duty over everyone operating under the brokerage.

question: Which of the following is an OREC office-identification sign requirement for a licensed broker's office and branch offices?
choice_a: The sign must be lit with neon at all times
choice_b: No sign is required if the office is inside the broker's residence
choice_c: The sign only needs to list the Commission's phone number
choice_d: The sign must contain the broker's or registered trade name, indicate the party is a real estate broker (e.g., using words like "realty" or "real estate"), in letters at least one inch high
explanation: Each licensed broker must erect and maintain a sign at the entrance of the office and each branch office containing the broker's or registered trade name, indicating the party is a real estate broker (not a private party), in letters not less than one inch in height.

question: Which of the following is listed among the Commission's examples of "untrustworthy, improper, fraudulent or dishonest dealing" tied to a broker-in-charge's supervisory duty?
choice_a: Lending a broker's license to an associate, permitting an associate to operate as a broker, or failure of a broker to properly supervise the activities of an associate
choice_b: A broker taking a paid vacation during the license term
choice_c: A broker declining a listing that is outside their specialty
choice_d: A broker referring a client to another firm for a referral fee disclosed in writing
explanation: The rules specifically classify lending a broker's license to an associate, permitting an associate to operate as a broker, or a broker's failure to properly supervise an associate's activities as prohibited, untrustworthy conduct.

question: Under the prohibited-dealings rule, what supervisory obligation does a broker have regarding everyone performing licensed activities under that broker?
choice_a: A broker has no duty to verify licensure status of persons working under them
choice_b: A broker must ensure that all persons performing real estate licensed activities under the broker are properly licensed
choice_c: This duty applies only to brokers who supervise more than ten associates
choice_d: The duty applies only at the time of hiring, not on an ongoing basis
explanation: Failure by a broker to ensure all persons performing real estate licensed activities under the broker are properly licensed is listed as a form of untrustworthy or improper dealing.

question: Under the prohibited-dealings rule, what restriction applies to an associate with respect to their broker's supervision?
choice_a: An associate may perform licensed activities independent of their broker's supervision if properly insured
choice_b: An associate may supervise their own transactions once they have three years of experience
choice_c: An associate shall not perform licensed activities outside their broker's supervision
choice_d: There is no supervision requirement for broker associates, only for sales associates
explanation: Rule 605:10-17-4(23) provides that an associate shall not perform licensed activities outside their broker's supervision, reinforcing the broker-in-charge's ongoing supervisory authority and liability.

question: When a formal disciplinary hearing is held regarding a complaint against a real estate associate or company, what is required of the supervising broker?
choice_a: The supervising broker has no role in the hearing
choice_b: Attendance is entirely optional with no consequence for absence
choice_c: Only the Commission's own staff may attend, not the supervising broker
choice_d: The supervising broker shall attend the formal hearing unless the Secretary-Treasurer provides written notice that attendance is not required; failure to attend may result in disciplinary action against the supervising broker
explanation: The supervising broker is required to attend all formal hearings in which their associate or company is the subject of a complaint, unless the Secretary-Treasurer gives written notice that attendance is not required; failing to attend may itself result in disciplinary action against the supervising broker.

question: A broker's license is suspended for misconduct. What automatically happens to the associates who were under that broker's supervision?
choice_a: The associates are automatically placed on inactive status for the duration of the suspension/revocation period, unless they request a transfer to another broker
choice_b: Nothing changes for the associates; they may continue working as before
choice_c: Those associates automatically become licensed brokers themselves
choice_d: The associates' licenses are automatically revoked as well
explanation: When a broker's license is suspended or revoked, associates under that broker's supervision are automatically placed inactive for the duration of the suspension/revocation period, unless the associate requests to be transferred to another broker.

question: If a suspended or revoked broker has a branch office, what generally happens to that branch office's license?
choice_a: The branch office is automatically transferred to a competitor firm
choice_b: The branch office license will be placed inactive, unless otherwise ordered by the Commission, and its associated licensees will automatically be placed inactive unless they request a transfer
choice_c: The branch office license is unaffected because it is a separate license
choice_d: The branch office is permanently revoked with no possibility of reopening
explanation: If a suspended/revoked broker has a branch office, the branch office license will be placed inactive (unless the Commission orders otherwise), and all licensees associated with the branch office will automatically be placed inactive for the suspension/revocation period unless they request a transfer to another broker.

question: A managing corporate broker is suspended for an act committed on behalf of the corporation. What is the effect on the corporation's own broker license?
choice_a: The corporation's license is unaffected since only the individual is disciplined
choice_b: The corporation must immediately dissolve
choice_c: The corporation's broker license will be placed inactive, unless otherwise ordered by the Commission, and its associates will automatically be placed inactive unless they request a transfer
choice_d: The corporation's license is automatically upgraded to a new managing broker with no filing
explanation: If a managing corporate broker is suspended or revoked for an act on behalf of the corporation, the corporation's broker license will be placed inactive unless the Commission orders otherwise, and all licensees associated with the corporation will automatically be placed inactive for the suspension/revocation period unless they request a transfer.

question: A branch office license has lapsed for two years, and the broker now wishes to reinstate it. What must be submitted?
choice_a: An entirely new original application, since any lapse voids the branch office
choice_b: Nothing; branch offices reinstate automatically after two years
choice_c: Only a letter notifying the Commission of intent to resume business
choice_d: The license fee(s) plus the reinstatement fee, forms, and documents required by the Commission
explanation: A branch office that has lapsed for less than three years and wishes to reinstate must submit the license fee(s) and the reinstatement fee, forms, and documents required by the Commission. Only a lapse of more than three years requires an original application as a new branch office.

question: A corporation's real estate license has lapsed for ninety days, and the corporation now seeks reinstatement. In addition to fees, forms, and documents, what additional item does the rule specifically require because the lapse exceeded sixty days?
choice_a: A current "Certification of Good Standing"
choice_b: A new criminal background check for every shareholder
choice_c: A notarized letter from the Governor's office
choice_d: Proof of liability insurance
explanation: For a corporation, association, or partnership that has lapsed for less than three years and lapsed for more than sixty days, reinstatement requires a current "Certification of Good Standing" in addition to the license fee(s) and reinstatement fee, forms, and documents.

question: A licensee holding a sales associate license wants to become a broker. Among the requirements of Section 858-303, what education-related item specifically relates to preparing a broker to supervise others?
choice_a: Completion of a 15-hour real estate photography course
choice_b: Completion of the Broker in Charge course as defined in the Code, in addition to 90 clock hours of advanced instruction
choice_c: A separate license exam limited to marketing law
choice_d: No supervisory-specific education is required to become a broker
explanation: An applicant for a broker license who holds a sales associate license (or is unlicensed) must, among other things, complete 90 clock hours of advanced real estate instruction and successfully complete the Broker in Charge course as defined in the Code.

question: An existing broker associate applies to upgrade to a (managing) broker license. Compared to an applicant who holds only a sales associate license, what is different about the education requirement?
choice_a: The broker associate must complete double the advanced-instruction hours
choice_b: The broker associate applicant is fully exempt from any additional education
choice_c: The broker associate applicant need only submit evidence of successful completion of the Broker in Charge course, rather than the full 90 clock hours of advanced instruction
choice_d: There is no difference; both must complete identical requirements
explanation: An applicant for a broker license who already holds a broker associate license must show two years of active licensure, submit evidence of successful completion of the Broker in Charge course, and document ten transactions — but is not required to complete the full 90-hour advanced course required of sales-associate applicants.

question: Under Commission rule, may a single broker act as the broker of record for more than one licensed firm?
choice_a: No, a broker may only ever be the broker for one firm
choice_b: Yes, without any location restriction whatsoever
choice_c: Only if both firms are corporations, never partnerships
choice_d: Yes, a broker may be the broker for more than one firm so long as the firms are at the same location
explanation: A broker may be the broker for more than one firm so long as the firms are at the same location, per the broker's operational-procedures rule.

question: A licensee sets up a personal corporation or LLC solely to receive commission payments from their broker, without the entity itself performing licensed acts. Under Commission rule, which of the following is a required condition for this arrangement to be permissible?
choice_a: The managing broker must provide approval to the Commission of the licensee's corporation or LLC, and the entity must not perform any act requiring a real estate license
choice_b: The entity may advertise using its own name to build a personal brand
choice_c: The entity may receive referral fees from any licensee, not just the associate's own broker
choice_d: The licensee need not hold an active individual real estate license
explanation: A licensee's personal corporation or LLC formed to receive compensation may not perform or hold itself out as performing licensed acts, may not advertise under its own name, and requires the managing broker's approval to the Commission; the licensee must also hold an active individual license and be the majority owner/president or member.
